title.en: Make the buried part of a spatial puzzle visible

summary: Give the player a way to see interior and hidden cells, because a three-dimensional puzzle hides most of its own state.
objective: Ensure the player can perceive the puzzle state they are asked to reason about.
applies_when: A puzzle has interior cells, stacked layers or occluded regions.
Pieces can be placed where they are not visible from outside.
The player must plan a route or a packing through a volume.
example_prompts: Let me see inside the packed tray to find the empty cells.
Show the maze one layer at a time.
negative_signals: Puzzles whose difficulty deliberately depends on hidden information.
Flat or single-layer boards where nothing is occluded.
not_for: Puzzles whose difficulty deliberately depends on hidden information.
Flat or single-layer boards where nothing is occluded.

principles: In a solid volume most cells are invisible, so a player asked to reason about the whole volume is being asked to plan with missing information.
Hiding by occlusion is not a difficulty design; it is an interface failure unless the hidden information is deliberately part of the puzzle.
Different questions need different reveals: finding a gap suits a slice or an empty-cell highlight, planning a route suits a layer view, and understanding a packing suits an exploded or ghosted view.
The reveal must not become a second state. Whatever is shown or hidden is a view, so the puzzle state and the legality of moves are unaffected.
implementation: Offer at least one reveal that matches the puzzle question: a movable slice, a layer selector, ghosting of outer pieces, or highlighting of empty cells.
Keep the reveal a pure view operation with no effect on placement, legality or completion.
Preserve orientation cues during the reveal so the player does not lose the mapping between the view and the volume.
Allow interaction in the revealed view where it is safe, and be explicit when placement is disabled in a particular mode.
Provide a way to see the whole volume again in one action.
observable_checks: Ask the player to find a single empty interior cell using the navigation the design intends. Judge the result against that workflow: an orbit-based inspection design passes if a short, purposeful rotation answers the question, while a design that offers a slice or a gap highlight should answer it without repeated searching.
Toggle every reveal mode and confirm the puzzle state and legality are unchanged.
Confirm orientation remains understandable when switching between full and sliced views.
Check that pieces placed in a revealed view are placed where the preview indicated.

creative_affordances: Reveal styles are open: transparency, wireframe, exploded layers or an x-ray band all work.
Deliberately hidden information is a valid design when the player knows it is hidden.
known_limits: Authored presentation guidance; no runtime puzzle has been play-tested for this record.
It offers no measure of puzzle difficulty or player performance.
